title: Three-tier prioritization, staffing, and comms blueprint
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working blueprint to organize the company-level priorities and resource asks for the coming 12 weeks. The goal is to (1) propose a compact set of company OKRs structured by three prioritized tiers, (2) list near-term hiring and backfill asks tied to measurable impact, and (3) outline the all-hands / exec-update cadence and comms plan to get alignment. This is intentionally short and action-focused; expect follow-ups and an operations worksheet with FTE-by-role estimates.

High-level framing: the three tiers
- Tier A (must-deliver): Reliability & cost stability. Keep the platform within budget and hit latency/uptime SLOs. If we don't solve this, product adoption stalls.
- Tier B (differentiation): Developer experience and developer velocity. Improve onboarding time, SDK stability, and the rollout/rollback UX. Drives acquisition and retention.
- Tier C (scale & market): Enterprise readiness & regional expansion (compliance, Private deployments, support model). Important for long-term revenue and enterprise deals.

Draft company OKRs (compact, measurable)
OKR 1 (Tier A) — Platform reliability and cost:
  - Objective: Reduce critical production incidents and bring unit cost stability under control
  - Key results (KR):
    * KR1.1: Reduce Sev2+ incidents impacting customer APIs from 9/month to <=3/month by quarter end
    * KR1.2: Achieve 95th p50 token latency <=120ms for hosted API across top-10 models
    * KR1.3: Reduce per-token cost variance to <10% month-over-month via batching and cache policies
  - Owner: eng-sre + serving-runtime lead

OKR 2 (Tier B) — Developer-first friction reduction:
  - Objective: Make Redwood the fastest path for engineers to ship LLM features
  - Key results:
    * KR2.1: Reduce median time-to-first-successful-call (signup->production call) from 3 days to <6 hours
    * KR2.2: Ship two SDK breaking-change-free releases with >95% test coverage and no regression alerts
    * KR2.3: Launch a curated quickstart template set (chat, embeddings, rerank) and drive 20% lift in new API trials converting to usage within 14 days
  - Owner: developer-experience + product-hosted-api

OKR 3 (Tier C) — Enterprise readiness and go-to-market enablement:
  - Objective: Deliver private deployment baseline and go-to-market artifacts for pilot customers
  - Key results:
    * KR3.1: Complete 3 private-deployment pilots with documented runbooks and automated onboarding scripts
    * KR3.2: Achieve SOC2 readiness gap assessment with remediation plan and timeline (90-day runway)
    * KR3.3: Close two enterprise pilot contracts for Dedicated offering with committed monthly reserved capacity
  - Owner: product-private-deployments + solutions-engineering

Staffing and prioritization asks (near term + rationale)
- Immediate (Q2 hires / reassignments):
  1) +2 SRE engineers (priority: incident reduction, observability). Impact: directly reduces MTTR and supports OKR1.
  2) +1 SDK engineer (developer DX) and +1 documentation/content engineer (quickstarts/templates). Impact: OKR2 time-to-value improvements.
  3) +1 Solutions Engineer for Private pilots (customer onboarding + runbook creation). Impact: closes pilot cadence for OKR3.
- Medium term (conditional on runway/bench):
  1) +1 infra automation engineer to accelerate autoscaling and bursting policies across Dedicated clusters.
  2) +1 product manager (private deployments) to coordinate pilots and compliance artifacts.

Headcount notes and alternatives:
- If we must pick only two hires, prioritize 2 SRE + 1 SDK engineer (i.e., shift a Solutions hire to a second SDK if revenue runway is tight). That gives material impact on both reliability and developer conversion.
- Consider 12-week contractor for documentation/quickstarts as cheaper near-term fix; convert to perm if conversion KPIs show improvement.

All-hands and exec-update plan (timelines & agenda)
- Two-week timeline to finalize OKRs for exec review:
  * Week 0 (this doc): circulate to exec and leads for comments
  * Week 1: Working session w/ eng leads + product to reconcile feasibility and exact KR targets
  * Week 2: Final exec sign-off; prepare talk tracks and slide deck for the all-hands
- All-hands suggested structure (45–60m):
  1) CEO top-level framing (7–10m): three-tier theme and why it matters now
  2) Engineering highlight (10–12m): progress on reliability, visible metrics, and the hiring asks
  3) Product & DX (8–10m): quickstarts, SDK plan, and early user signals
  4) Customer stories / pilot recap (6–8m): 1–2 short customer vignettes (ops team)
  5) Fireside Q&A (10–12m): pre-collected + live, moderated by Head of People or comms
  6) Slack follow-up thread + pinned FAQ doc
- Exec update (for board and C-suite): single-page memo + top-3 asks (headcount, runway, pilot closures). Include a one-slide metric dashboard (incidents, latency, MRR trends, trial->pay conversion).

Comms and stakeholder enablement
- Comms owner: Head of Comms (Priya to draft) with support from People and Product Marketing.
- Pre-all-hands prep: collect 2–3 short customer quotes (solutions eng), 3 charts (SRE, SDK, sales pipeline), and 1 cost-impact slide.
- Post-all-hands: publish short recap and link to action tracker; leaders must update assigned tickets within 72 hours.

Contingency and fallback plays
- If incident reduction doesn't hit threshold by week 6, enable a squad-level red team to run focused blameless postmortems and isolation drills; temporary pause on non-critical feature launches.
- If hiring approvals delayed >30 days, activate contractor pool and reduce scope for non-essential DX work (deprioritize new templates in favor of improving core quickstart).

Open questions and unresolved tradeoffs
- Exact numerical thresholds for KR1.2 latency target: is 120ms p50 aggressive for top-10 models across regions? Should we make model-specific targets?
- How much of the hiring cost can be absorbed from unspent contractor budget vs new headcount? Finance input needed (JIRA-OPS-678).
- Do we consolidate private deployment pilots under a single cross-functional owner or keep them distributed across solution leads?

Immediate next steps (owners and dates)
- By 2025-02-12: Product + SRE to produce feasibility notes on KRs (Devon + Luca).
- By 2025-02-14: Comms draft for all-hands and one-slide exec memo (Priya).
- By 2025-02-18: Exec working session to lock targets and approve hires to request to Finance (Ava).
- By 2025-02-24: Draft all-hands deck produced; rehearsal scheduled with CEO and leads.

Quick checklist (scratch):
- [ ] Collect customer quotes (solutions eng)
- [ ] Finalize hiring priority list and cost estimates
- [ ] Produce three dashboard charts for all-hands
- [ ] Draft exec memo and run it by CFO
- [ ] Schedule rehearsal and slide review

Notes to reviewers:
- This remains a draft. Please add comments inline or tag the doc owner. Focus feedback on: KR measurability, hire prioritization, and the all-hands narrative (tone + timing).

-- end --
